For every exponent \(5^j\) with \(j\ge 1\), we have
\[
5^j \equiv 5 \pmod{20}.
\]
Since \(2^{20}\equiv 1 \pmod{25}\), each term satisfies
\[
2^{5^j}\equiv 2^5\equiv 7 \pmod{25}.
\]
Also each term is divisible by \(4\). The unique residue mod \(100\) that is \(0\pmod 4\) and \(7\pmod{25}\) is \(32\). Thus every term is \(32\pmod{100}\).

There are \(2015\) terms, so
\[
N\equiv 2015\cdot 32 \equiv 64480 \equiv 80 \pmod{100}.
\]
\[
\boxed{80}
\]
